title: Monomial-ratio uniformizers and exhaustion of boundary primes
statement:
Let $G$ be a free abelian group of finite rank and let $P\subseteq G$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid generating $G$ as a group, with $P\cap(-P)=\{0\}$. Let $I$ be a finite set and let $
u_i:G	o\mathbf Z$ be surjective homomorphisms such that
$$P=\{g\in G:
u_i(g)\ge0	ext{ for all }i\in I\}.$$
For each $i$ fix $f_i\in P$ with $
u_i(f_i)=0$ and $
u_j(f_i)>0$ for every $j
e i$. Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $z:P	o R$ satisfy $z^0=1$, $z^{q+q'}=z^qz^{q'}$ and $z^q
e0$ for all $q$. Put $\mathfrak p_i=(z^q:
u_i(q)>0)R$ and assume each $\mathfrak p_i$ is prime and satisfies $z^q\in\mathfrak p_i\Longleftrightarrow
u_i(q)>0$. Then the $\mathfrak p_i$ are distinct nonzero primes. For each $i$ and each $e_i\in G$ with $
u_i(e_i)=1$, there is $N_i\ge0$ such that $e_i+N_i f_i\in P$ and
$$\pi_i=z^{e_i+N_i f_i}/z^{N_i f_i}\in A_i=R_{\mathfrak p_i}$$
is nonzero, belongs to the maximal ideal, and generates that ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For every $q\in P$, writing $m=
u_i(q)$ and $g=q-me_i$, there is $M\ge0$ such that $g+Mf_i\in P$, $
u_i(g+Mf_i)=0$, and
$$u_q=z^{g+Mf_i}/z^{Mf_i}\in A_i^	imes,\qquad z^q=u_q\pi_i^m.$$
The ring $A_i$ is a Noetherian local domain and a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Its normalized additive valuation satisfies $v_i(z^q)=
u_i(q)$. Each $\mathfrak p_i$ has height one, meaning that it is nonzero and there is no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak p_i$. Every prime of $R$ containing a chart monomial contains some $\mathfrak p_i$; consequently the height-one primes containing a chart monomial are exactly these $\mathfrak p_i$. If $I=\varnothing$, the hypotheses force $P=G=0$ and no prime contains any chart monomial.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, the half-space description gives $P=G$. Sharpness then gives $G=P=\{0\}$. The only chart monomial is $z^0=1$, which belongs to no prime. Henceforth assume $I\ne\varnothing$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A_i$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p_iA_i$. Since $z^{b_i}\notin\mathfrak p_i$, the fraction $\pi_i=z^{a_i}/z^{b_i}$ lies in this ideal. The fraction relation shows $R\hookrightarrow A_i\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(R)$: a denominator is outside the proper prime and hence nonzero, and $r/s=0$ forces $ur=0$ for some nonzero $u$, thus $r=0$. Consequently $A_i$ is a domain and $\pi_i\ne0$. Its fraction field is $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, because every fraction of $R$ is a quotient of elements of $A_i$, and conversely fractions of elements of $A_i\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ remain in that field.

The equality $q+d+mb_i=c+ma_i$ in $G$ is an equality between elements of $P$. Multiplicativity gives $z^qz^d(z^{b_i})^m=z^c(z^{a_i})^m$. Dividing by the displayed nonzero denominators in $A_i$ proves $z^q=u_q\pi_i^m$. This includes $m=0$, and $

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak p_iA_i$ is generated by the images of the monomials with $\nu_i(q)>0$: extending an ideal generated by a set allows the same finite sums with coefficients in $A_i$. By Step 4, each such generator is $\pi_i(u_q\pi_i^{\nu_i(q)-1})$, hence lies in $(\pi_i)$. Step 3 gives the reverse containment. Thus the maximal ideal is exactly $(\pi_i)$, with its generator nonzero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to $R$ and the multiplicative set $R\setminus\mathfrak p_i$ to see that $A_i$ is Noetherian. The fraction construction of Step 3 has all three localization properties in that statement. Now [lem-sc-principal-ideal-dvr] applies: $A_i$ is a Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal generated by the nonzero $\pi_i$. Thus it is a DVR, and $\pi_i$ is a uniformizer as defined in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

Let $v_i$ be the normalized additive valuation of this DVR on its fraction field, identified with $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ in Step 3. It is nonnegative on nonzero elements of $A_i$, and $v_i(\pi_i)=1$. A unit $u$ has value zero: $0=v_i(uu^{-1})=v_i(u)+v_i(u^{-1})$ and both summands are nonnegative. Apply the multiplication and power identities of [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic] to Step 4 to obtain $v_i(z^q)=0+m=\nu_i(q)$; for $m=0$ the same assertion follows directly from $z^q=u_q$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $\dim A_i=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], this is the supremum of lengths of prime chains below $\mathfrak p_i$. Since $R$ is a domain, $(0)$ is prime, and Step 2 gives $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p_i$. A prime strictly between these would give a chain of length two, contradicting that supremum. Thus each $\mathfrak p_i$ has height one in precisely the stated sense.

proof.text: If $Q$ additionally has height one, $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p_i\subseteq Q$ forces $Q=\mathfrak p_i$ by the stipulated no-intermediate-prime meaning of height one. Conversely, each $\mathfrak p_i$ has height one by Step 8 and contains the chart monomial $z^{a_i}$ from Step 2. Together with Step 1 this proves the exact classification and every degenerate clause.
